Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Vertex Capital Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Vertex Capital Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are John Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Grant, Head of Distribution; and David Patel, Head of Operations.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to John Harlan.

John Harlan: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3 2024. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust market appreciation in equities and alternatives, coupled with our ninth consecutive quarter of positive net long-term flows totaling $28 billion year-to-date. Our AUM grew to a record $1.45 trillion.

Sarah Chen: Thank you, John. From a financial perspective, Vertex Capital Management delivered strong results in Q3 2024. Our revenue was $1.42 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by organic AUM expansion, resilient fee dynamics, and higher-margin inflows into our alternatives and active equity platforms. Our expenses were managed tightly at $980 million, resulting in net income of $320 million. Our expense ratio improved to 35 basis points due to scale efficiencies from technology investments and optimized compensation structures.

Let me expand on our capital allocation strategy, which remains central to delivering superior total shareholder returns. With $1.45 trillion in AUM—up 14% year-over-year on those $28 billion in net inflows—our balance sheet is strong, featuring $4.2 billion in cash and equivalents, net debt to EBITDA of 1.2x, and return on invested capital above 18%. This enables a disciplined approach across three pillars: shareholder returns, growth investments, and financial flexibility.

On shareholder returns, we've generated 22% annualized TSR over five years, surpassing peers like T. Rowe Price and BlackRock on a risk-adjusted basis. In Q3, we repurchased $450 million in shares—2.1 million shares at an average of $215, or 1.8% of float—bringing year-to-date buybacks to $1.2 billion, or 85% of our $1.4 billion authorization. Our buyback yield is now 3.2% trailing twelve months, paired with an 8% dividend increase to $0.65 per share, yielding 1.2% forward. Free cash flow conversion hit 92% this quarter at $320 million, with FY24 expected at $1.3 billion; fee-related earnings cover dividends 3.5x, supporting a 40-45% payout while buying back opportunistically below 12x forward FRE. We'll seek a new $1.5 billion authorization in Q1 2025 if valuations stay attractive against our 15-17% organic AUM growth path.

For growth investments, we deployed $280 million in Q3 across technology, product innovation, and seeding. On tech, $150 million year-to-date went into VertexNext, our AI-enhanced risk analytics platform—tailored for multi-asset active strategies, incorporating NLP for 50,000+ earnings transcripts and satellite data for commodity ETFs. It's cut portfolio drift 25% in our $180 billion active equity mandates and operational costs by 15 bps. We're piloting blockchain settlement with State Street for T+0 execution in our $250 billion ETF suite by mid-2025, aiming for 5-10 bps fee advantages over low-cost rivals.

Product innovation took $80 million, seeding a $750 million private credit fund at 9-11% net IRRs in senior direct lending to middle-market tech—40% deployed with CalPERS and OMERS commitments; a $400 million ESG transition equity fund for EU Taxonomy-aligned industrials amid 22% YTD sustainable inflows and CSRD tailwinds; and a $300 million Asia ex-Japan small-cap active ETF for high-beta EM push.

Regionally, North America is 62% of AUM at $900 billion with 8% organic growth via wirehouses like Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch. Europe at 18% or $260 billion grew 22% on UCITS and MiFID III, including a €120 million London quant boutique acquisition—accretive 200 bps to EPS year one. APAC at 15% or $220 billion surged 28% YoY with $12 billion inflows to our Singapore alternatives platform amid China stabilization and India capex; $100 million more in FY25 for Mumbai and Tokyo onshore mandates targeting 20% AUM share by 2027.

M&A is opportunistic post our $1.1 billion Pinnacle Alternatives deal adding $120 billion in privates, lifting alternatives to 28%. We're eyeing 15-20 bolt-ons in credit and infrastructure with strict 12-15% IRR, >1.5x synergies, and culture fit hurdles.

Financial flexibility keeps net leverage under 1.5x with $4.2 billion liquidity, including $1.8 billion undrawn revolvers—ready for outflows like our negligible -0.5% in fixed income or dislocations akin to 2022 LDI.

Our framework uses a 15% ROIC hurdle across scenarios: base 12% AUM growth, bear 5%, bull 20%. Trends like the $84 trillion wealth transfer, $12 trillion ETF AUM, and 15% alts penetration guide 55% to returns, 35% growth, 10% flexibility. Amid 4.1% 10-year yields, 19x equity multiples, and Middle East risks, we're overweight fixed income duration, underweight China consumer, overweight US AI capex in $90 billion tech mandates. FY24 capex $450-500 million, 60% tech, for 300-400 bps margin expansion to 42% by 2026. Since 2020, 65% capital returned to shareholders, 25% ROIC on growth.

Turning to AUM and flow guidance, Q4 2023 closed at $1.45 trillion, up 12% YoY and 4% QoQ—ninth straight growth quarter. Equities $650 billion (45%), fixed income $325 billion (up 8%), alternatives $220 billion (18% YoY fastest), multi-asset $180 billion, cash $75 billion. U.S. $870 billion (60%) on $28 billion 401(k)/IRA flows; Europe $290 billion (10% up) on UCITS ETFs; APAC $185 billion (15% up) via HK/Singapore; EM ex-Asia $80 billion; Canada/other $25 billion.

2023 long-term net inflows $72 billion—strongest since 2021, Q4 $22 billion beating guide 10%. Retail/RIA $40 billion (55%), institutional $25 billion, ETFs $7 billion to $150 billion total. Passive/smart-beta 60%, active equities $12 billion (AI/clean energy +300bps), ESG $18 billion (25%), minor outflows from legacy FI.

Q1 2024 guide: $18-24 billion inflows, assuming 2-4% markets, Fed at 5.25-5.50%. Upside from 401(k) rebalancing, new Global AI Equity ETF ($500 million seed, $5 billion YE target). FY24: $75-90 billion inflows for 8-10% organic growth, $1.65-1.75 trillion AUM at 5-7% appreciation. Retail 50-55%, institutional 30-35%, ETFs 15%; alts $25-30 billion. Tokenization on ApexChain for $5 billion tokenized assets.

Pillars: tech scale via Aladdin upgrade (GenAI flows, -15% churn); five Q1 ETFs (19bps active-ESG FI, Nasdaq covered-call); $200 million APAC hiring, Temasek infra partnerships, AIFMD 2.0 wrappers. Fees steady 42bps, 1-2bps compression, 38-40% margins.

On net flow drivers, Q3 long-term inflows $12.4 billion, YTD $28.7 billion—22% YoY up, 4.2% organic vs. industry 2.8%. Fund performance key: 68% strategies beat benchmarks 1Y (vs 55% Q2). Vista Alpha Equity 18.2% (+420bps S&P), $4.1 billion flows; Core Plus Bond 6.8% YTD (+110bps Agg), $3.2 billion; private credit 11.5% IRR, $2.8 billion. Quant ML cut tracking error <1.5%. EM outflows $800 million addressed via India/ASEAN rotation.

Market trends: small/mid-cap rotation (Russell +12%, VSMG ETF $1.9 billion); FI surge on yield dip to 3.85%, $5.6 billion; ESG FI +28% to $42 billion; cash outflows $1.1 billion, crypto +$400 million. New active ETFs $2.7 billion seed/inflows; robo 150k accounts $1.8 billion. North America $7.7 billion (62%), EMEA $3.2 billion, APAC $2.9 billion (45% up), LatAm $600 million.

Q4 guide $10-14 billion on rebalancing, cuts, private interval fund. ClientFlow AI +18% cross-sell, 120 RFPs at 65% conversion.

Management fees $1.42 billion, +8% YoY/+5% QoQ on $650 billion AUM (+12% YoY), 7.2% organic, 4.8% markets. Equities $742 million (52%, +11%), FI $385 million (+6%), alts $185 million (+12%). Institutional $950 million (+10%), retail $470 million (+4%). Fee rate 43.5bps (-10bps YoY, stable QoQ): ETFs 22% mix, alts 85bps sticky.

Offsets: tiered schedules (2bps pass-through), new active ETFs ($2.5 billion at 25bps), Aligned Incentives (20% fees to hurdles, 98% retention, +5bps). Americas 44bps stable, EMEA 42bps (-15bps MiFID), APAC 48bps (+15%). ApexNext SMAs +10bps tax-alpha; perf fee pilots +3bps. Focus alts 20% AUM by 2026, ESG/thematics 60bps, EM active +400bps. Q2 fees $1.45-1.50 billion, 43-44bps.

Compensation ratio 51.2% Q4/50.8% FY23 on $1.85 billion Q4/$7.1 billion FY revenues (+22%/+16%). Vs peers: BlackRock 48%, T. Rowe 53%. Fixed 28%, variable 22.8% (bonus +15% on 78% Lipper beat, 12% organic). Deferred equity 60% RSUs TSR-linked. Americas 52% (45 hires incl PineBridge), Europe 48% Dublin hub, APAC 55% (30 advisors). AI ApexQuant 2.0 -15% workflows/8 heads; RPA 10% back-office; ESG deferrals 40%. New hedge-like for PMs, 94% retention. FY24 50-51%, ROE 22%.

Our expense improvements stem from these efficiencies, positioning us for ongoing margin expansion.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Sarah. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in active equities and private credit. We're navigating the current market environment by overweighting US AI capex themes, extending duration selectively in fixed income amid stabilizing yields, and rotating from China consumer into India and ASEAN amid EM dispersion. We launched the VertexNext AI-enhanced platform and three new seeded strategies this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $2.7 billion in initial inflows and top-quartile Morningstar rankings across 68% of mandates, driving client retention above 98%.

Lisa Grant: Thank you, Michael. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF and alternatives funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC and Europe are paying off, as evidenced by 28% YoY AUM growth in APAC on $12 billion inflows and 22% in Europe via UCITS demand, alongside retail platforms like Schwab and Fidelity delivering $40 billion year-to-date through our WealthTech integrations and thematic launches.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure, including $150 million into VertexNext for AI risk analytics and blockchain pilots targeting T+0 settlement, resulting in 25% less portfolio drift, 15 bps cost compression, and 15% churn reduction via GenAI flows. This has increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on RPA for back-office automation and data lake consolidation for personalized reporting, compressing our expense ratio while scaling to support $75-90 billion FY24 inflows.

John Harlan: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes client-centric growth targeting $40 billion institutional and 8-10% retail via robo-hybrid; product innovation with three Q1 active ETFs (AI semis, private credit interval, ESG EM debt) and evergreen PE to $50 billion; operational excellence via $250 million tech for AI optimization, tokenization unlocking $10 billion, expense to 32 bps; and sustainable resilience with 42% ESG AUM, climate transition funds, robust stress testing. Mid-teens AUM to $620-650 billion by 2025 YE, 12-15% revenue growth, ROE to 22%.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Morningstar.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your AUM and flow guidance for upcoming periods?

Sarah Chen: Good morning, Emily. As detailed earlier, we're guiding Q1 2024 net long-term inflows of $18 to $24 billion, accelerating from Q4, with FY24 at $75 to $90 billion for 8-10% organic growth to $1.65-1.75 trillion AUM. This assumes moderate market returns, Fed stability, and no shocks, with upside from new AI ETF and 401(k) flows, resilience from our active/passive mix.

Emily Carter: Thank you. And a follow-up on drivers of net flows, particularly fund performance versus market trends?

Lisa Grant: Absolutely. Performance led with 68% outperformance, like Alpha Equity +420bps driving $4.1 billion, alongside trends like small-cap rotation ($1.9 billion to VSMG) and ESG FI surges. New ETFs and robo added momentum, with APAC up 45% YoY.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with Goldman Sachs.

David Kim: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of your private credit strategies?

Michael Torres: Good morning, David. Our private credit platform delivered 11.5% annualized net IRR, attracting $2.8 billion commitments from pensions, with the new $750 million fund 40% deployed to tech lending at 9-11% targets. Quant models optimized selection, complementing broader alts growth to 28% of AUM.

David Kim: And how is the new VertexNext platform performing relative to expectations?

David Patel: Exceeding expectations—25% portfolio drift reduction across $180 billion equities, 15 bps op cost savings, and blockchain pilots on track for mid-2025 T+0 in ETFs, enhancing competitiveness.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Lee with Barclays.

Rachel Lee: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

David Patel: Certainly, Rachel. Beyond VertexNext, RPA via UiPath cut back-office staff 10%, AI automated 15% quant research for 2% comp gains, and ClientFlow AI boosted cross-sell 18%. These drive our 35 bps expense ratio toward 32 bps, supporting margin expansion.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to John Harlan for closing remarks.

John Harlan: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Vertex Capital Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
